semantics.label: Contextual fact
semantics.description: A contextual fact is recorded; no favourable or adverse polarity, never scored.

response_meaning.RECORDED: The contextual fact has been recorded with its provenance.
response_meaning.NOT_AVAILABLE: The contextual fact could not be obtained; the reason is recorded.

semantics.label: Control effectiveness — design
semantics.description: Design-only control question; operating evidence is not required.

response_meaning.NO: The control is absent, or so weak in design that it cannot be relied upon.
response_meaning.YES: The control is appropriately designed and proportionate to this entity's risk, nature, size and complexity.
response_meaning.PARTIALLY: Material design gaps leave residual weakness.
response_meaning.NOT_APPLICABLE: The activity the control addresses is genuinely not undertaken, so the control cannot exist.

semantics.label: Control effectiveness — design and operating
semantics.description: Both design adequacy and operating effectiveness must hold for a favourable response.

response_meaning.NO: The control is absent, or so weak in design or operation that it cannot be relied upon.
response_meaning.YES: The control is appropriately designed and operated effectively over the relevant period or sample.
response_meaning.PARTIALLY: Material design gaps or evidenced operating exceptions leave residual weakness.
response_meaning.NOT_APPLICABLE: The activity the control addresses is genuinely not undertaken, so the control cannot exist.

semantics.label: Control effectiveness — operating
semantics.description: Operating-effectiveness control question; period, sample or system evidence is required.

response_meaning.NO: The control is absent, or so weak in operation that it cannot be relied upon.
response_meaning.YES: The control operated effectively over the relevant period or sample, evidenced by period data, samples or system facts.
response_meaning.PARTIALLY: Evidenced exceptions in operation leave residual weakness.
response_meaning.NOT_APPLICABLE: The activity the control addresses is genuinely not undertaken, so the control cannot exist.

semantics.label: Inherent exposure
semantics.description: Response meaning for inherent ML/TF exposure questions.

response_meaning.NO: The exposure characteristic is absent or immaterial for the assessment period.
response_meaning.YES: The exposure characteristic is present and material to the entity, judged against the materiality criteria in the guidance.
response_meaning.PARTIALLY: The exposure characteristic exists but is limited, bounded or below the materiality criteria.
response_meaning.NOT_APPLICABLE: The underlying activity is genuinely not undertaken in the assessment period (not: unknown, unevidenced or unanswered).

question_detail.prompt: Cross-border or corridor activity is concentrated in a small number of jurisdictions or corridors (contextual fact — not scored).
question_detail.guidance: Record the largest single corridor share, the top-three share and the risk classification of those corridors. Concentration in lower-risk corridors is not adverse; concentration in higher-risk corridors amplifies IR-GEO-01 and is judged there. Share thresholds are configuration parameters ([MAT_CORRIDOR_TOP1_SHARE], [MAT_CORRIDOR_TOP3_SHARE]), not fixed wording.

rows.title: Adopt the exposure -> control -> residual -> judgement -> response chain, with question classes
rows.rationale: Reference design approved by the platform methodology owner (MIPL) for the AML-CFT-RBA v1.1 reference catalogue. Reference approval only: it does not constitute approval by any regulator and does not authorise use in a live supervisory decision until the regulator adopts it.
rows.decision_text: Adopt the chain, and adopt the CORE / CONDITIONAL / ENHANCED question-class model so that a catalogue question is not automatically mandatory in every assessment.

rows.title: Inherent question set: 17 inherent questions across 6 dimensions — 12 CORE / 5 CONDITIONAL — 16 scored / 1 contextual non-scored
rows.rationale: Reference design approved by the platform methodology owner (MIPL) for the AML-CFT-RBA v1.1 reference catalogue. Reference approval only: it does not constitute approval by any regulator and does not authorise use in a live supervisory decision until the regulator adopts it.
rows.decision_text: Adopt the red-teamed set. `IR-BUS-03` (outsourced/intragroup AML operations) is moved to control effectiveness (`THIRD_PARTY_OVERSIGHT`); `IR-TRX-02` merges into `IR-PRD-02` (cash) and `IR-TRX-03` into `IR-GEO-02` (cross-border); `IR-DEL-03` merges into `IR-DEL-01`/`IR-PRD-03`; `IR-GEO-03` (corridor concentration) is recorded as a contextual, non-scored fact because concentration in lower-risk corridors is not higher inherent exposure. Every remaining scored inherent question satisfies: `YES` = more inherent ML/TF exposure before controls.

rows.title: Control question set: 53 questions across 20 dimensions (36 CORE, 11 CONDITIONAL, 6 ENHANCED)
rows.rationale: Reference design approved by the platform methodology owner (MIPL) for the AML-CFT-RBA v1.1 reference catalogue. Reference approval only: it does not constitute approval by any regulator and does not authorise use in a live supervisory decision until the regulator adopts it.
rows.decision_text: Adopt with the closure changes: `CT-DQ-02` retired (reconciliation absorbed by `CT-DQ-01` and `CT-TM-02`); `CT-IT-03` narrowed to board reporting so closure validation is assessed once, in `CT-REM-03`; file/alert/report sampling and training-effectiveness testing (`CT-CDD-03`, `CT-ALRT-02`, `CT-STRI-03`, `CT-STRG-03`, `CT-TRN-03`, `CT-REM-03`) classified ENHANCED (examination/thematic); third-party oversight and model governance classified CONDITIONAL on the presence of third parties or automated detection.

rows.title: Context-sensitive response semantics per axis and effectiveness focus
rows.rationale: Reference design approved by the platform methodology owner (MIPL) for the AML-CFT-RBA v1.1 reference catalogue. Reference approval only: it does not constitute approval by any regulator and does not authorise use in a live supervisory decision until the regulator adopts it.
rows.decision_text: Adopt `INHERENT_SEM`, `CONTROL_SEM_DESIGN`, `CONTROL_SEM_OPERATING`, `CONTROL_SEM_DESIGN_AND_OPERATING` and `CONTEXT_FACT_SEM`. A pure DESIGN question must not require operating evidence merely because a global control definition demanded it.

rows.title: Selective design vs operating-effectiveness split (14 DESIGN / 27 OPERATING / 12 DESIGN_AND_OPERATING)
rows.rationale: Reference design approved by the platform methodology owner (MIPL) for the AML-CFT-RBA v1.1 reference catalogue. Reference approval only: it does not constitute approval by any regulator and does not authorise use in a live supervisory decision until the regulator adopts it.
rows.decision_text: Adopt as catalogued; split only where the operating failure mode is distinct.

rows.title: Evidence basis (replaces the "observation + one evidence item per question" mandate)
rows.rationale: Reference design approved by the platform methodology owner (MIPL) for the AML-CFT-RBA v1.1 reference catalogue. Reference approval only: it does not constitute approval by any regulator and does not authorise use in a live supervisory decision until the regulator adopts it.
rows.decision_text: Every **final supervisory response** must carry (A) a rationale/observation appropriate to the judgement and (B) a sufficient **governed evidence basis**. An evidence basis may be an `ENTERPRISE_DOCUMENT`, `SYSTEM_FACT`, `REGULATORY_RETURN`, `STRUCTURED_METRIC`, `SUPERVISORY_SAMPLE`, `WORKPAPER`, `PRIOR_EXAMINATION`, `FINDING`, `REMEDIATION_RECORD`, `RFI_RESPONSE` or `AUTHORISED_EXTERNAL_SOURCE`. One document or governed fact may support several questions; a question need not create a duplicate evidence object. For purely system-factual questions, structured provenance (source, period, timestamp, extraction reference) satisfies the evidence requirement. No assertion-only favourable conclusion. No AML-local document store; references are governed references into existing platform records.

rows.title: N/A discipline: enumerated conditions only, rationale always required; N/A distinguished from NOT_TRIGGERED and NOT_ASKED
rows.rationale: Reference design approved by the platform methodology owner (MIPL) for the AML-CFT-RBA v1.1 reference catalogue. Reference approval only: it does not constitute approval by any regulator and does not authorise use in a live supervisory decision until the regulator adopts it.
rows.decision_text: Adopt. `NOT_APPLICABLE` (activity genuinely not undertaken), `NOT_TRIGGERED` (conditional trigger absent) and `NOT_ASKED` / `OUT_OF_SCOPE` (enhanced question outside this assessment's scope) are three distinct states; none may silently score zero or full, and none is a favourable response.

rows.title: Legacy `STR_SAR_GOVERNANCE`: governed audited relink to `STR_GOVERNANCE` (supersedes the display-only recommendation)
rows.rationale: Reference design approved by the platform methodology owner (MIPL) for the AML-CFT-RBA v1.1 reference catalogue. Reference approval only: it does not constitute approval by any regulator and does not authorise use in a live supervisory decision until the regulator adopts it.
rows.decision_text: If the methodology owner confirms that `STR_SAR_GOVERNANCE` is the semantic predecessor of `STR_GOVERNANCE`, execute a **governed, audited, idempotent relink** of the 22 rows to canonical `STR_GOVERNANCE`, preserving the original dimension code and provenance, assessment status, responses, judged ratings and history. Because the rows hold no responses and no calculated results, no rating is invented. Display/lineage-only mapping is rejected as a final route: it leaves LINK-11 permanently open and is therefore not an acceptable certification path.

rows.title: Global AML/CFT core plus sector applicability/overlay capability (supersedes the single-catalogue-with-N/A approach)
rows.rationale: Reference design approved by the platform methodology owner (MIPL) for the AML-CFT-RBA v1.1 reference catalogue. Reference approval only: it does not constitute approval by any regulator and does not authorise use in a live supervisory decision until the regulator adopts it.
rows.decision_text: Adopt a **global core** (44 CORE_ALL, 4 CORE_WITH_SECTOR_GUIDANCE) with **13 SECTOR_CONDITIONAL** questions resolved by trigger and **9 SECTOR_OVERLAY_CANDIDATE** questions (correspondent/remittance corridors, virtual-asset and complex products, agent networks, automated detection and model governance) earmarked for sector overlays. Overlays should later be expressed as sector-scoped applicability and guidance records over the same canonical question catalogue, resolved through the existing entity-context methodology resolver — duplicating no question text, evidence contract, document or storage architecture. Sectors analysed: banks, credit unions, insurance, securities, MSBs, VASPs, DNFBPs, other.

rows.title: v1.0 -> v1.1 transition, by assessment status
rows.rationale: Reference design approved by the platform methodology owner (MIPL) for the AML-CFT-RBA v1.1 reference catalogue. Reference approval only: it does not constitute approval by any regulator and does not authorise use in a live supervisory decision until the regulator adopts it.
rows.decision_text: APPROVED / SUPERSEDED v1.0 assessments are never re-versioned and remain reproducible. DRAFT v1.0 assessments may be abandoned or superseded and recreated under v1.1 through a governed, audited process where the supervisor decides that is appropriate. SUBMITTED / REVIEWED v1.0 assessments require an explicit supervisory decision per assessment: finish under v1.0, or return/cancel and restart under v1.1. Never silently re-version. No migration in this wave.
